message.content: We don’t have a definitive “largest planet” in the entire universe—our knowledge is limited to what we can observe from Earth. Among the planets we’ve discovered outside our Solar System (exoplanets), the biggest ones are often called “super‑Jupiters.” One of the most massive and inflated exoplanets known is **HD 100546 b**, which has a radius roughly 2–3 times that of Jupiter and a mass several times larger. However, because many exoplanets are still being discovered and their properties refined, it’s possible that even larger planets exist that we haven’t yet observed.
